rendered: The clinical sepsis samples were serum from septic patients infected with these bacteria: E. coli[1] and E. faecium[2]. The study used independent serum samples from enrolled subjects, including septic patients with confirmed E. coli[3] and septic patients with confirmed E. faecium infection[4]. The control group was healthy volunteers serving as the control[5], so the control was healthy human serum rather than a second pathogen or a different infection. The LDA in the clinical-sample panel separates the E. coli, E. faecium and Healthy groups. Fig. 5[6]
